questions.text: Let $A=\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 100\}$ and R be a relation on A such that $R=\{(a, b): a=2b+1\}$. Let $(a_1, a_2), (a_2, a_3), (a_3, a_4), \ldots, (a_k, a_{k+1})$ be a sequence of k elements of R such that the second entry of an ordered pair is equal to the first entry of the next ordered pair. Then the largest integer k, for which such a sequence exists, is equal to :
questions.sol:
Each term is obtained from the next by $a_i=2a_{i+1}+1$, so the chain is longest when it ends at $a_{k+1}=1$.
Working back: $1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63$; the next would be $127>100$.
Pairs: $(3,1), (7,3), (15,7), (31,15), (63,31)$, so $k=5$.

questions.text:
If the system of equations
$2x+\lambda y+3z=5$
$3x+2y-z=7$
$4x+5y+\mu z=9$
has infinitely many solutions, then $(\lambda^2+\mu^2)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The first two equations are independent, so the third must equal $p(\text{first})+q(\text{second})$.
$x$: $2p+3q=4$; constants: $5p+7q=9$. Hence $q=2$, $p=-1$.
$y$: $-\lambda+4=5$, so $\lambda=-1$; $z$: $-3-2=\mu$, so $\mu=-5$.
$\lambda^2+\mu^2=1+25=26$.

questions.text: The number of terms of an A.P. is even; the sum of all the odd terms is 24, the sum of all the even terms is 30 and the last term exceeds the first by $\dfrac{21}{2}$. Then the number of terms which are integers in the A.P. is :
questions.sol:
Let there be $2n$ terms with common difference $d$. Each even term exceeds the preceding odd term by $d$, so $nd=30-24=6$.
Also $(2n-1)d=\dfrac{21}{2}$. Dividing, $\dfrac{2n-1}{n}=\dfrac74$, so $n=4$ and $d=\dfrac32$.
Odd terms: $4a+12d=24$ gives $a=\dfrac32$.
The terms are $\dfrac32, 3, \dfrac92, 6, \dfrac{15}{2}, 9, \dfrac{21}{2}, 12$: four integers.

questions.text: The number of ways, in which the letters A, B, C, D, E can be placed in the 8 boxes of the figure below so that no row remains empty and at most one letter can be placed in a box, is :
questions.sol:
The rows have 3, 3 and 2 boxes. Choose 5 of the 8 boxes so that every row is used.
All choices: $\binom85=56$. Leaving a 3-box row empty: $\binom55=1$ way for each such row (2 in all); leaving the 2-box row empty: $\binom65=6$. Two rows cannot both be empty.
Valid choices $=56-8=48$; arranging the 5 letters: $48\times5!=5760$.

questions.text:
Given three indentical bags each containing 10 balls, whose colours are as follows :
RedBlueGreen
Bag I325
Bag II433
Bag III514
A person chooses a bag at random and takes out a ball. If the ball is Red, the probability that it is from bag I is p and if the ball is Green, the probability that it is from bag III is q, then the value of $\left(\dfrac1p+\dfrac1q\right)$ is :
questions.sol:
Bags are equally likely and each holds 10 balls, so by Bayes' theorem the probabilities are proportional to the counts.
Red: $p=\dfrac{3}{3+4+5}=\dfrac14$. Green: $q=\dfrac{4}{5+3+4}=\dfrac13$.
$\dfrac1p+\dfrac1q=4+3=7$.

questions.text: Let the area of the triangle formed by a straight line L : $x+by+c=0$ with co-ordinate axes be 48 square units. If the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the line L makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the positive $x$-axis, then the value of $b^2+c^2$ is :
questions.sol:
In normal form the line is $x\cos45^\circ+y\sin45^\circ=p$, i.e. $x+y=\sqrt2p$, so $b=1$.
$x+y+c=0$ cuts the axes at $(-c, 0)$ and $(0, -c)$; area $\dfrac{c^2}{2}=48$, so $c^2=96$.
$b^2+c^2=97$.

questions.text: Let the point P of the focal chord PQ of the parabola $y^2=16x$ be $(1, -4)$. If the focus of the parabola divides the chord PQ in the ratio $m:n$, $\gcd(m, n)=1$, then $m^2+n^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$a=4$, focus $S(4, 0)$. $P=(at^2, 2at)$ with $t=-\dfrac12$; the other end has parameter $-\dfrac1t=2$, so $Q=(16, 16)$.
Focal distances: $SP=1+4=5$, $SQ=16+4=20$.
$m:n=1:4$, so $m^2+n^2=17$.

questions.text: If $\theta\in\left[-\dfrac{7\pi}{6}, \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right]$, then the number of solutions of $\sqrt3\,\mathrm{cosec}^2\theta-2\left(\sqrt3-1\right)\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta-4=0$, is equal to :
questions.sol:
Discriminant $=4(\sqrt3-1)^2+16\sqrt3=4(\sqrt3+1)^2$, so $\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta=\dfrac{(\sqrt3-1)\pm(\sqrt3+1)}{\sqrt3}=2$ or $-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$.
$\sin\theta=\dfrac12$: $\theta=-\dfrac{7\pi}{6}, \dfrac\pi6, \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ (3 values).
$\sin\theta=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$: $\theta=-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}, -\dfrac\pi3, \dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ (3 values).
Total 6.

questions.text: If the image of the point P$(1, 0, 3)$ in the line joining the points A$(4, 7, 1)$ and B$(3, 5, 3)$ is Q$(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Points of AB: $(4-t, 7-2t, 1+2t)$, direction $(-1, -2, 2)$.
For the foot F: $(3-t, 7-2t, 2t-2)\cdot(-1, -2, 2)=9t-21=0$, so $t=\dfrac73$ and $F=\left(\dfrac53, \dfrac73, \dfrac{17}{3}\right)$.
$Q=2F-P=\left(\dfrac73, \dfrac{14}{3}, \dfrac{25}{3}\right)$, so $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=\dfrac{46}{3}$.

questions.text: The line $L_1$ is parallel to the vector $\vec{a}=-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and passes through the point $(7, 6, 2)$ and the line $L_2$ is parallel to the vector $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and passes through the point $(5, 3, 4)$. The shortest distance between the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ is :
questions.sol:
$\vec a\times\vec b=(2, 17, -7)$, of magnitude $\sqrt{342}=3\sqrt{38}$.
Joining vector $(5-7, 3-6, 4-2)=(-2, -3, 2)$; its dot product with $\vec a\times\vec b$ is $-4-51-14=-69$.
Shortest distance $=\dfrac{69}{3\sqrt{38}}=\dfrac{23}{\sqrt{38}}$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ and a vector $\vec{c}$ be such that $(\vec{a}-\vec{c})\times\vec{b}=-18\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}=3$. If $\vec{b}\times\vec{c}=\vec{d}$, then $\left|\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}\right|$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\vec a\times\vec b=(-17, -7, 13)$.
$\vec c\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec b-(-18, -3, 12)=(1, -4, 1)$, so $\vec d=\vec b\times\vec c=(-1, 4, -1)$.
$\vec a\cdot\vec d=-2-12-1=-15$, so $|\vec a\cdot\vec d|=15$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\cos(2x)+a\cos(4x)-b}{x^4}$ is finite, then $(a+b)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\cos2x=1-2x^2+\dfrac23x^4-\cdots$ and $\cos4x=1-8x^2+\dfrac{32}{3}x^4-\cdots$.
The numerator is $(1+a-b)-(2+8a)x^2+\cdots$; for a finite limit both brackets vanish: $a=-\dfrac14$, $b=\dfrac34$.
$a+b=\dfrac12$.

questions.text: $\displaystyle4\int_0^1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+x^2}+\sqrt{1+x^2}}\right)dx-3\log_e\left(\sqrt3\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Rationalise: the integrand is $\dfrac{\sqrt{3+x^2}-\sqrt{1+x^2}}{2}$, so the first term is $2\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(\sqrt{3+x^2}-\sqrt{1+x^2}\right)dx$.
Using $\displaystyle\int\sqrt{x^2+k}\,dx=\frac x2\sqrt{x^2+k}+\frac k2\log\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+k}\right)$:
$\displaystyle\int_0^1\sqrt{3+x^2}\,dx=1+\frac34\log_e3$ and $\displaystyle\int_0^1\sqrt{1+x^2}\,dx=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}+\frac12\log_e(1+\sqrt2)$.
Expression $=2+\dfrac32\log_e3-\sqrt2-\log_e(1+\sqrt2)-\dfrac32\log_e3=2-\sqrt2-\log_e(1+\sqrt2)$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $(a, b)$ be the point of intersection of the curve $x^2=2y$ and the straight line $y-2x-6=0$ in the second quadrant. Then the integral $I=\displaystyle\int_a^b\frac{9x^2}{1+5^x}\,dx$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$x^2=2(2x+6)$ gives $x^2-4x-12=0$, so $x=6$ or $-2$; in the second quadrant the point is $(-2, 2)$.
Adding $I$ to itself with $x\to-x$: $2I=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}9x^2\left(\frac{1}{1+5^x}+\frac{5^x}{1+5^x}\right)dx=\int_{-2}^{2}9x^2\,dx=48$.
$I=24$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:[1, \infty)\to[2, \infty)$ be a differentiable function. If $\displaystyle10\int_1^xf(t)\,dt=5xf(x)-x^5-9$ for all $x\ge1$, then the value of $f(3)$ is :
questions.sol:
At $x=1$: $0=5f(1)-10$, so $f(1)=2$.
Differentiating: $10f=5f+5xf^\prime-5x^4$, i.e. $xf^\prime-f=x^4$, so $\left(\dfrac fx\right)^\prime=x^2$.
$\dfrac fx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+C$ with $2=\dfrac13+C$, $C=\dfrac53$.
$f(3)=3\left(9+\dfrac53\right)=32$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the set of all $a\in\mathbf{R}-\{1\}$, for which the roots of the equation $(1-a)x^2+2(a-3)x+9=0$ are positive is $(-\infty, -\alpha]\cup[\beta, \gamma)$, then $2\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Real roots: $4(a-3)^2-36(1-a)\ge0$, i.e. $a^2+3a\ge0$, so $a\le-3$ or $a\ge0$.
Product $\dfrac{9}{1-a}>0$ needs $a<1$; then sum $\dfrac{-2(a-3)}{1-a}>0$ needs $a<3$.
Set: $(-\infty, -3]\cup[0, 1)$, so $\alpha=3$, $\beta=0$, $\gamma=1$ and $2\alpha+\beta+\gamma=7$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the sum of the first 10 terms of the series $\dfrac{4\cdot1}{1+4\cdot1^4}+\dfrac{4\cdot2}{1+4\cdot2^4}+\dfrac{4\cdot3}{1+4\cdot3^4}+\cdots$ is $\dfrac mn$, where $\gcd(m, n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$1+4r^4=(2r^2+1)^2-(2r)^2=(2r^2-2r+1)(2r^2+2r+1)$, so
$\dfrac{4r}{1+4r^4}=\dfrac{1}{2r^2-2r+1}-\dfrac{1}{2r^2+2r+1}$, and $2r^2+2r+1$ is the first denominator with $r$ replaced by $r+1$.
The sum telescopes: $1-\dfrac{1}{2\cdot100+20+1}=\dfrac{220}{221}$, so $m+n=441$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $y=\cos\left(\dfrac\pi3+\cos^{-1}\dfrac x2\right)$, then $(x-y)^2+3y^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let $\theta=\cos^{-1}\dfrac x2$, so $x=2\cos\theta$, $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{4-x^2}}{2}$, and $y=\dfrac x4-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\sqrt{4-x^2}$.
Then $4y-x=-\sqrt3\sqrt{4-x^2}$; squaring, $16y^2-8xy+x^2=12-3x^2$, i.e. $4x^2-8xy+16y^2=12$.
So $x^2-2xy+4y^2=(x-y)^2+3y^2=3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let A$(4, -2)$, B$(1, 1)$ and C$(9, -3)$ be the vertices of a triangle ABC. Then the maximum area of the parallelogram AFDE, formed with vertices D, E and F on the sides BC, CA and AB of the triangle ABC respectively, is __________.
questions.sol:
Area of ABC $=\dfrac12\left|4(1+3)+1(-3+2)+9(-2-1)\right|=6$.
If $AF=t\cdot AB$ with $FD\parallel AC$, then $AE=(1-t)AC$ and the parallelogram has area $2t(1-t)\times[\mathrm{ABC}]$, largest at $t=\dfrac12$.
Maximum area $=\dfrac12\times6=3$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y\sec^2x=2\sec^2x+3\tan x\cdot\sec^2x$ such that $y(0)=\dfrac54$. Then $12\left(y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)-e^{-2}\right)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Integrating factor $e^{2\tan x}$. With $t=\tan x$: $ye^{2t}=\displaystyle\int(2+3t)e^{2t}\,dt=e^{2t}\left(\frac14+\frac{3t}{2}\right)+C$.
$y=\dfrac14+\dfrac32\tan x+Ce^{-2\tan x}$; $y(0)=\dfrac54$ gives $C=1$.
$y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)=\dfrac74+e^{-2}$, so $12\left(y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)-e^{-2}\right)=21$.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) Heat capacity of body(I) J kg$^{-1}$
(B) Specific heat capacity of body(II) J K$^{-1}$
(C) Latent heat(III) J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$
(D) Thermal conductivity(IV) J m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Heat capacity $=\dfrac{Q}{\Delta T}$: J K$^{-1}$ (II).
(B) Specific heat capacity $=\dfrac{Q}{m\Delta T}$: J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ (III).
(C) Latent heat $=\dfrac Qm$: J kg$^{-1}$ (I).
(D) Thermal conductivity, from $\dfrac{Q}{t}=KA\dfrac{\Delta T}{L}$: J m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ (IV).

questions.text: Given a charge q, current I and permeability of vacuum $\mu_0$. Which of the following quantity has the dimension of momentum ?

questions.text: The moment of inertia of a circular ring of mass M and diameter r about a tangential axis lying in the plane of the ring is :
questions.sol:
The radius is $R=\dfrac r2$. About a diameter $I=\dfrac12MR^2$; by the parallel axis theorem, about a tangent in the plane $I=\dfrac32MR^2$.
$I=\dfrac32M\dfrac{r^2}{4}=\dfrac38Mr^2$.

questions.text:
A body of mass 1 kg is suspended with the help of two strings making angles as shown in figure. Magnitudes of tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$, respectively, are (in N) :
(Take acceleration due to gravity 10 m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
$T_1$ makes $60^\circ$ and $T_2$ makes $30^\circ$ with the horizontal.
Horizontal: $T_1\cos60^\circ=T_2\cos30^\circ$, so $T_1=\sqrt3T_2$.
Vertical: $T_1\sin60^\circ+T_2\sin30^\circ=10$, i.e. $\dfrac32T_2+\dfrac12T_2=10$, so $T_2=5$ N and $T_1=5\sqrt3$ N.

questions.sol:

questions.text: Two water drops each of radius 'r' coalesce to form a bigger drop. If 'T' is the surface tension, the surface energy released in this process is :
questions.sol:
Volume is conserved: $R^3=2r^3$, so $R=2^{1/3}r$.
Energy released $=T\left(2\cdot4\pi r^2-4\pi R^2\right)=4\pi r^2T\left[2-2^{2/3}\right]$.

questions.text:
Identify the characteristics of an adiabatic process in a monoatomic gas.
(A) Internal energy is constant.
(B) Work done in the process is equal to the change in internal energy.
(C) The product of temperature and volume is a constant.
(D) The product of pressure and volume is a constant.
(E) The work done to change the temperature from $T_1$ to $T_2$ is proportional to $(T_2-T_1)$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
With $Q=0$, $\Delta U=-W$: the work equals the change in internal energy in magnitude (B), and $W=nC_V(T_1-T_2)$ is proportional to $(T_2-T_1)$ (E).
The internal energy changes because the temperature changes, so (A) is false.
The constants are $TV^{\gamma-1}$ and $PV^\gamma$, not $TV$ or $PV$, so (C) and (D) are false.

questions.text: An electron with mass 'm' with an initial velocity $(t=0)$ $\vec{v}=v_0\hat{i}\ (v_0>0)$ enters a magnetic field $\vec{B}=B_0\hat{j}$. If the initial de-Broglie wavelength at $t=0$ is $\lambda_0$ then its value after time 't' would be :
questions.sol:
The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so it does no work and the speed stays $v_0$.
The momentum magnitude is unchanged, so $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{mv_0}=\lambda_0$.

questions.text: A sinusoidal wave of wavelength 7.5 cm travels a distance of 1.2 cm along the $x$-direction in 0.3 sec. The crest P is at $x=0$ at $t=0$ sec and maximum displacement of the wave is 2 cm. Which equation correctly represents this wave ?
questions.sol:
$k=\dfrac{2\pi}{7.5}=0.84$ cm$^{-1}$ and speed $=\dfrac{1.2}{0.3}=4$ cm/s, so $\omega=kv=3.35$ s$^{-1}$.
A crest at $x=0$, $t=0$ needs a cosine with zero phase: $y=2\cos(0.83x-3.35t)$ cm.

questions.text: Two identical objects are placed in front of convex mirror and concave mirror having same radii of curvature of 12 cm, at same distance of 18 cm from the respective mirrors. The ratio of sizes of the images formed by convex mirror and by concave mirror is :
questions.sol:
$|f|=6$ cm, $u=-18$ cm.
Convex ($f=+6$): $\dfrac1v=\dfrac16+\dfrac1{18}$, $v=4.5$ cm, $|m|=\dfrac{4.5}{18}=\dfrac14$.
Concave ($f=-6$): $\dfrac1v=-\dfrac16+\dfrac1{18}$, $v=-9$ cm, $|m|=\dfrac{9}{18}=\dfrac12$.
Ratio $=\dfrac{1/4}{1/2}=\dfrac12$.

questions.text: A bi-convex lens has radius of curvature of both the surfaces same as $1/6$ cm. If this lens is required to be replaced by another convex lens having different radii of curvatures on both sides $(R_1\neq R_2)$, without any change in lens power then possible combination of $R_1$ and $R_2$ is :
questions.sol:
For the same material the power depends on $\dfrac1{R_1}+\dfrac1{R_2}$ (magnitudes, both surfaces convex). Originally this is $6+6=12$ cm$^{-1}$.
Options: $6+9=15$, $3+3=6$, $5+7=12$, $3+7=10$.
So $\dfrac15$ cm and $\dfrac17$ cm.

questions.text:
Energy released when two deuterons $\left({}_1\mathrm{H}^2\right)$ fuse to form a helium nucleus $\left({}_2\mathrm{He}^4\right)$ is :
(Given : Binding energy per nucleon of ${}_1\mathrm{H}^2=1.1$ MeV and binding energy per nucleon of ${}_2\mathrm{He}^4=7.0$ MeV)
questions.sol:
Binding energy of He-4 $=4\times7.0=28.0$ MeV; of two deuterons $=2\times2\times1.1=4.4$ MeV.
Energy released $=28.0-4.4=23.6$ MeV.

questions.text: In the digital circuit shown in the figure, for the given inputs the P and Q values are :
questions.sol:
Both inputs are 1. The NAND gate gives $\overline{1\cdot1}=0$; each input through a NOT gate gives 0, and the OR of these is 0.
The AND gate receives the NAND output 0, so $P=0$.
The last NOT gate receives a 0 and gives 1, so the final NOR gate has an input 1 and $Q=0$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Net dipole moment of a polar linear isotropic dielectric substance is not zero even in the absence of an external electric field.
Reason (R) : In absence of an external electric field, the different permanent dipoles of a polar dielectric substance are oriented in random directions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol:
Without an external field, thermal agitation keeps the permanent dipoles randomly oriented (R is correct), so their moments cancel and the net dipole moment is zero.
Hence (A) is not correct but (R) is correct.

questions.text: Two large plane parallel conducting plates are kept 10 cm apart as shown in figure. The potential difference between them is V. The potential difference between the points A and B (shown in the figure) is :

The field between the plates is uniform, $E=\dfrac{V}{0.10\ \mathrm{m}}$, perpendicular to the plates.
In the right triangle ACB, AC $=3$ cm (parallel to the plates) and AB $=5$ cm, so CB $=4$ cm along the field.
$V_{AB}=E\times0.04=\dfrac{0.04}{0.10}V=\dfrac25V$.

questions.text: A solenoid having area A and length '$l$' is filled with a material having relative permeability 2. The magnetic energy stored in the solenoid is :
questions.sol:
Energy density in a medium of permeability $\mu=\mu_r\mu_0=2\mu_0$ is $\dfrac{B^2}{2\mu}=\dfrac{B^2}{4\mu_0}$.
Energy $=\dfrac{B^2}{4\mu_0}\times Al=\dfrac{B^2Al}{4\mu_0}$.

questions.text: Consider a circular loop that is uniformly charged and has a radius $a\sqrt2$. Find the position along the positive $z$-axis of the cartesian coordinate system where the electric field is maximum if the ring was assumed to be placed in $xy$ plane at the origin :
questions.sol:
On the axis, $E=\dfrac{kQz}{(R^2+z^2)^{3/2}}$. Setting $\dfrac{dE}{dz}=0$: $R^2+z^2=3z^2$, so $z=\dfrac{R}{\sqrt2}$.
With $R=a\sqrt2$, $z=a$.

questions.text:
In a moving coil galvanometer, two moving coils $M_1$ and $M_2$ have the following particulars :
$R_1=5\ \Omega$, $N_1=15$, $A_1=3.6\times10^{-3}$ m$^2$, $B_1=0.25$ T
$R_2=7\ \Omega$, $N_2=21$, $A_2=1.8\times10^{-3}$ m$^2$, $B_2=0.50$ T
Assuming that torsional constant of the springs are same for both coils, what will be the ratio of voltage sensitivity of $M_1$ and $M_2$ ?
questions.sol:
Voltage sensitivity $=\dfrac{NAB}{kR}$.
$M_1$: $\dfrac{15\times3.6\times10^{-3}\times0.25}{5}=2.7\times10^{-3}$; $M_2$: $\dfrac{21\times1.8\times10^{-3}\times0.50}{7}=2.7\times10^{-3}$ (each divided by the same $k$).
Ratio $1:1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A wheel of radius 0.2 m rotates freely about its center when a string that is wrapped over its rim is pulled by force of 10 N as shown in figure. The established torque produces an angular acceleration of 2 rad/s$^2$. Moment of intertia of the wheel is __________ kg m$^2$.
(Acceleration due to gravity $=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Torque $=FR=10\times0.2=2$ N m $=I\alpha$.
$I=\dfrac{2}{2}=1$ kg m$^2$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text:
A satellite of mass 1000 kg is launched to revolve around the earth in an orbit at a height of 270 km from the earth's surface. Kinetic energy of the satellite in this orbit is __________ $\times10^{10}$ J.
(Mass of earth $=6\times10^{24}$ kg, Radius of earth $=6.4\times10^6$ m, Gravitational constant $=6.67\times10^{-11}$ N m$^2$ kg$^{-2}$)
questions.sol:
Orbit radius $r=6.4\times10^6+0.27\times10^6=6.67\times10^6$ m.
$KE=\dfrac{GMm}{2r}=\dfrac{6.67\times10^{-11}\times6\times10^{24}\times10^3}{2\times6.67\times10^6}=3\times10^{10}$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The length of a light string is 1.4 m when the tension on it is 5 N. If the tension increases to 7 N, the length of the string is 1.56 m. The original length of the string is __________ m.
questions.sol:
Extension is proportional to tension: $L=L_0+cT$.
$1.4=L_0+5c$ and $1.56=L_0+7c$ give $c=0.08$ m/N and $L_0=1.0$ m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A ray of light suffers minimum deviation when incident on a prism having angle of the prism equal to $60^\circ$. The refractive index of the prism material is $\sqrt2$. The angle of incidence (in degrees) is __________.
questions.sol:
At minimum deviation $r=\dfrac A2=30^\circ$, and $\sin i=\mu\sin r=\sqrt2\times\dfrac12=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$.
$i=45^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The internal energy of air in $4\ \mathrm{m}\times4\ \mathrm{m}\times3$ m sized room at 1 atmospheric pressure will be __________ $\times10^6$ J.
(Consider air as diatomic molecule)
questions.sol:
For a diatomic gas $U=\dfrac52nRT=\dfrac52PV$.
$U=2.5\times1.013\times10^5\times48\approx1.22\times10^7$ J $\approx12\times10^6$ J.

questions.text:
'$x$' g of NaCl is added to water in a beaker with a lid. The temperature of the system is raised from 1°C to 25°C. Which out of the following plots, is best suited for the change in the molarity (M) of the solution with respect to temperature ?
[Consider the solubility of NaCl remains unchanged over the temperature range]
questions.sol:
Molarity $=\dfrac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{volume of solution}}$; the moles are fixed, so M varies inversely with the volume.
Water contracts from 1°C to 4°C (maximum density at about 4°C) and then expands.
So the molarity first rises slightly, reaches a maximum near 4°C and then falls steadily: the first plot.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are true ?
(A) The subsidiary quantum number $l$ describes the shape of the orbital occupied by the electron.
(B) The diagram shown in the figure is the boundary surface diagram of the $2p_x$ orbital.
(C) The $+$ and $-$ signs in the wave function of the $2p_x$ orbital refer to charge.
(D) The wave function of $2p_x$ orbital is zero everywhere in the $xy$ plane.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) True: $l$ fixes the shape of the orbital.
(B) True: the $2p_x$ boundary surface is two lobes along the $x$-axis, as drawn.
(C) False: the signs give the phase of the orbital function, not charge.
(D) False: the nodal plane of $2p_x$ is the $yz$ plane; in the $xy$ plane the function is non-zero away from the $y$-axis.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Arrange the following in order of magnitude of work done by the system/on the system at constant temperature.
(a) $|w_{\text{reversible}}|$ for expansion in infinite stages.
(b) $|w_{\text{irreversible}}|$ for expansion in single stage.
(c) $|w_{\text{reversible}}|$ for compression in infinite stages.
(d) $|w_{\text{irreversible}}|$ for compression in single stage.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Between the same two states, reversible expansion and reversible compression involve the same magnitude of work, $nRT\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}$, so $c=a$.
A single-stage expansion against the final (low) pressure does less work than this; a single-stage compression by the final (high) pressure needs more.
Order: $d>c=a>b$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of thermodynamic properties of Haber's process ?
questions.sol:
For $\mathrm{N_2+3H_2\rightarrow2NH_3}$, $\Delta H^\theta\approx-92$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^\theta\approx-198$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, both nearly constant with temperature.
So $-\dfrac{\Delta H^\theta}{T}$ is positive (about 300 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ near room temperature) and falls as T rises.
$-\dfrac{\Delta G^\theta}{T}=-\dfrac{\Delta H^\theta}{T}+\Delta S^\theta$ is about 200 lower: near 100 at first, falling through zero at higher T.
The second graph shows exactly this (with $\Delta H^\theta\approx-100$ and $\Delta S^\theta\approx-200$ as horizontal lines).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following chemical equilibrium of the gas phase reaction at a constant temperature : $\mathrm{A(g)\rightleftharpoons B(g)+C(g)}$
If p being the total pressure, $K_p$ is the pressure equilibrium constant and $\alpha$ is the degree of dissociation, then which of the following is true at equilibrium ?
options: If p value is extremely high compared to $K_p$, $\alpha\approx1$
If $K_p$ value is extremely high compared to p, $\alpha$ becomes much less than unity
questions.sol:
With 1 mol A initially, moles at equilibrium are $1-\alpha$, $\alpha$, $\alpha$ (total $1+\alpha$).
$K_p=\dfrac{\alpha^2p}{1-\alpha^2}$, so $\alpha=\sqrt{\dfrac{K_p}{K_p+p}}$.
$\alpha$ decreases as p increases; $\alpha\to0$ when $p\gg K_p$ and $\alpha\to1$ when $K_p\gg p$. Only the first statement is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Reactant A converts to product D through the given mechanism (with the net evolution of heat) :
A $\rightarrow$ B, slow; $\Delta H=+$ve
B $\rightarrow$ C, fast; $\Delta H=-$ve
C $\rightarrow$ D, fast; $\Delta H=-$ve
Which of the following represents the above reaction mechanism ?
questions.sol:
The slow first step has the highest activation barrier, and B lies above A (endothermic).
The two fast steps have small barriers, each going downhill (C below B, D below C).
Overall heat is evolved, so D lies below A.
Only the first profile shows all of these.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which among the following molecules is (a) involved in $sp^3d$ hybridization, (b) has different bond lengths and (c) has lone pair of electrons on the central atom ?
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{PF_5}$: $sp^3d$, unequal axial and equatorial bonds, but no lone pair.
$\mathrm{XeF_2}$: $sp^3d$ with three lone pairs, but both Xe$-$F bonds are axial and equal.
$\mathrm{XeF_4}$: $sp^3d^2$.
$\mathrm{SF_4}$: $sp^3d$, one lone pair (see-saw), with different axial and equatorial S$-$F bond lengths.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Electronic configuration of four elements A, B, C and D are given below :
(A) $1s^22s^22p^3$, (B) $1s^22s^22p^4$, (C) $1s^22s^22p^5$, (D) $1s^22s^22p^2$
Which of the following is the correct order of increasing electronegativity (Pauling's scale) ?
questions.sol:
A is N, B is O, C is F and D is C.
Electronegativity rises across period 2: C (2.5) < N (3.0) < O (3.5) < F (4.0).
Order: D < A < B < C.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: The nature of oxide $\left(\mathrm{TeO_2}\right)$ and hydride $\left(\mathrm{TeH_2}\right)$ formed by Te, respectively, are :
questions.sol:
Down group 16 the +4 state becomes less stable relative to lower states, so $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is a reducing agent while $\mathrm{TeO_2}$ acts as an oxidising agent.
The acidic character of the hydrides increases from $\mathrm{H_2O}$ to $\mathrm{H_2Te}$ (weaker E$-$H bonds), so $\mathrm{TeH_2}$ is acidic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The d-orbital electronic configuration of the complex among $\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{[Zn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$ that has the highest CFSE is :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$: $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ $d^6$ with strong-field en, low spin $t_{2g}^6e_g^0$, CFSE $-2.4\Delta_o$.
$\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$: high spin $t_{2g}^4e_g^2$, $-0.4\Delta_o$. $\mathrm{[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$: $t_{2g}^3e_g^2$, zero. $\mathrm{[Zn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$: $t_{2g}^6e_g^4$, zero.
Highest CFSE: $t_{2g}^6e_g^0$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The type of hybridization and the magnetic property of $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$ are,
questions.sol:
Mn is +3 ($3d^4$). $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ is a weak-field ligand, so the 3d electrons stay unpaired and the outer 4d orbitals are used: $sp^3d^2$.
Four unpaired electrons: paramagnetic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Formation of $\mathrm{Na_4[Fe(CN)_5NOS]}$, a purple coloured complex formed by addition of sodium nitroprusside in sodium carbonate extract of salt indicates the presence of :
questions.sol:
Sulphide ion reacts with sodium nitroprusside: $\mathrm{S^{2-}+[Fe(CN)_5NO]^{2-}\rightarrow[Fe(CN)_5NOS]^{4-}}$, a purple (violet) complex.
So the test shows the presence of sulphide ion.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
(Purification technique)		List - II
(Mixture of organic compounds)
(A) Distillation (simple)(I) Diesel + Petrol
(B) Fractional distillation(II) Aniline + Water
(C) Distillation under reduced pressure(III) Chloroform + Aniline
(D) Steam distillation(IV) Glycerol + Spent-lye
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Simple distillation separates liquids with very different boiling points: chloroform and aniline (III).
(B) Fractional distillation separates liquids with close boiling points, as in petroleum fractions: diesel and petrol (I).
(C) Glycerol decomposes at its boiling point, so it is recovered from spent lye under reduced pressure (IV).
(D) Aniline is steam volatile and immiscible with water: steam distillation (II).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.5 gram of an organic compound gave 60 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound (Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mm Hg) is __________%.
questions.sol:
Pressure of dry $\mathrm{N_2}$ $=715-15=700$ mm Hg.
Volume at STP $=60\times\dfrac{700}{760}\times\dfrac{273}{300}=50.3$ mL.
Mass of $\mathrm{N_2}$ $=\dfrac{28\times50.3}{22400}=0.0629$ g, so % N $=\dfrac{0.0629}{0.5}\times100=12.57$.

questions.text: In 3,3-dimethylhex-1-en-4-yne, there are _____$sp^3$, _____$sp^2$ and _____$sp$ hybridised carbon atoms respectively.
questions.sol:
The structure is $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}C(CH_3)_2{-}C{\equiv}C{-}CH_3}$.
$sp^3$: C-3, its two methyl carbons and C-6 (4). $sp^2$: C-1 and C-2 (2). $sp$: C-4 and C-5 (2).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Neopentane forms only one monosubstituted derivative.
Statement (II) : Melting point of neopentane is higher than n-pentane.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
All 12 hydrogens of neopentane, $\mathrm{C(CH_3)_4}$, are equivalent, so there is one monosubstituted product. Statement I is correct.
The compact, symmetrical neopentane molecules pack well in the crystal: m.p. about $-17$°C against about $-130$°C for n-pentane. Statement II is correct.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Two aryl halide molecules coupled by sodium in dry ether to give biphenyl: Fittig reaction (III).
(B) Diazonium salt with Cu/HCl giving ArCl: Gattermann reaction (IV).
(C) $\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}$ with NaI in dry acetone giving $\mathrm{C_2H_5I}$: Finkelstein reaction (II).
(D) A tertiary alcohol with $\mathrm{HCl/ZnCl_2}$ giving the chloride: Lucas reaction (I).

questions.text:
Consider the following reactions. From these reactions which reaction will give carboxylic acid as a major product ?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Mild acid hydrolysis of a nitrile stops at the amide.
(B) A Grignard reagent adds to $\mathrm{CO_2}$; hydrolysis gives RCOOH.
(C) $\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}$ then hydrolysis (Stephen reaction) gives the aldehyde RCHO.
(D) PCC oxidises a primary alcohol only to the aldehyde.
(E) Rosenmund reduction gives benzaldehyde, which bromine water oxidises to benzoic acid.
So B and E only.

questions.text:
When a concentrated solution of sulphanilic acid and 1-naphthylamine is treated with nitrous acid (273 K) and acidified with acetic acid, the mass (g) of 0.1 mole of product formed is :
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16, S : 32)
questions.sol:
Sulphanilic acid is diazotised and the diazonium ion couples with 1-naphthylamine to give the azo dye $\mathrm{HO_3S{-}C_6H_4{-}N{=}N{-}C_{10}H_6{-}NH_2}$.
Formula $\mathrm{C_{16}H_{13}N_3O_3S}$: $192+13+42+48+32=327$ g mol$^{-1}$.
0.1 mol weighs 32.7 g, i.e. about 33 g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A tetrapeptide, "$x$" on complete hydrolysis produced glycine (Gly), alanine (Ala), valine (Val), leucine (Leu) in equimolar proportion each. The number of tetrapeptides (sequences) possible involving each of these amino acids is :
questions.sol:
Each of the four different amino acids appears once, and a peptide sequence is ordered (N- to C-terminus).
Number of sequences $=4!=24$.

questions.text:
For the reaction A $\rightarrow$ B the following graph was obtained. The time required (in seconds) for the concentration of A to reduce to 2.5 g L$^{-1}$ (if the initial concentration of A was 50 g L$^{-1}$) is __________. (Nearest integer)
Given : $\log2=0.3010$
questions.sol:
From the graph the concentration halves in equal times (40 g L$^{-1}$ at 5 s, 20 g L$^{-1}$ at 15 s and 10 g L$^{-1}$ at 25 s), so the reaction is first order with $t_{1/2}=10$ s.
$t=\dfrac{2.303\,t_{1/2}}{0.693}\log\dfrac{50}{2.5}=\dfrac{10}{\log2}\log20=\dfrac{10\times1.3010}{0.3010}=43.2$ s.
Answer 43.

questions.text:
When 1 g each of compounds AB and $\mathrm{AB_2}$ are dissolved in 15 g of water separately, they increased the boiling point of water by 2.7 K and 1.5 K respectively. The atomic mass of A (in amu) is __________ $\times10^{-1}$ (Nearest integer)
(Given : Molal boiling point elevation constant is 0.5 K kg mol$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
$M=\dfrac{K_b\times w}{\Delta T_b\times W}$ with $w=1$ g and $W=0.015$ kg.
AB: $M=\dfrac{0.5}{2.7\times0.015}=12.35$; $\mathrm{AB_2}$: $M=\dfrac{0.5}{1.5\times0.015}=22.22$.
$a+b=12.35$ and $a+2b=22.22$ give $b=9.88$ and $a=2.47=24.7\times10^{-1}$, i.e. 25.

questions.text:
The spin-only magnetic moment value of $\mathrm{M^{n+}}$ ion formed among Ni, Zn, Mn and Cu that has the least enthalpy of atomisation is __________. (in nearest integer)
Here n is equal to the number of diamagnetic complexes among $\mathrm{K_2[NiCl_4]}$, $\mathrm{[Zn(H_2O)_6]Cl_2}$, $\mathrm{K_3[Mn(CN)_6]}$ and $\mathrm{[Cu(PPh_3)_3I]}$
questions.sol:
Zn (filled 3d, weak metallic bonding) has the least enthalpy of atomisation.
$\mathrm{K_2[NiCl_4]}$: tetrahedral $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$, 2 unpaired. $\mathrm{[Zn(H_2O)_6]Cl_2}$: $d^{10}$, diamagnetic. $\mathrm{K_3[Mn(CN)_6]}$: low-spin $d^4$, 2 unpaired. $\mathrm{[Cu(PPh_3)_3I]}$: $\mathrm{Cu^+}$ $d^{10}$, diamagnetic. So $n=2$.
$\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ is $d^{10}$ with no unpaired electrons: spin-only moment 0.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the above sequence of reactions. 151 g of 2-bromopentane is made to react. Yield of major product P is 80% whereas Q is 100%.
Mass of product Q obtained is __________g.
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, O : 16, Br : 80)
questions.sol:
2-Bromopentane, $\mathrm{C_5H_{11}Br}$ (151 g mol$^{-1}$): 151 g is 1 mol.
Alcoholic KOH gives mainly pent-2-ene (P, Saytzeff product): 0.80 mol.
Bromine adds to give 2,3-dibromopentane (Q, $\mathrm{C_5H_{10}Br_2}$, 230 g mol$^{-1}$): 0.80 mol $\times230=184$ g.
